subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Women Banned From Coffeehouses
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Women Banned From Coffeehouses.

hook.text: For centuries, coffeehouses were men-only spaces. Women were explicitly excluded—and they protested.

buildup.text: A 1674 London pamphlet, 'The Women's Petition Against Coffee,' complained husbands spent all day in coffeehouses.

discovery.text: The petition joked that coffee made men impotent. But the real grievance was exclusion from public intellectual life.

twist.text: Ottoman, European, and colonial coffeehouses all enforced male-only rules. The pattern was global, not local.

climax.text: It took until the late 1800s for women to regularly access café culture—and even then, only in certain progressive cities.

punchline.text: Coffeehouses built democracy—then excluded half the population from it.

quiz.question: What was the 1674 'Women's Petition Against Coffee' really about?
options: Women's exclusion from public intellectual life in coffeehouses
